findings.message: Both major findings from review-6-qa (r6) are resolved. Diffing story.r6.json against story.r7.json: exactly two passages were added (the-quick-slip, the-slow-slip) and exactly three were edited (how-to-go-down, last-look-at-the-gate, watch-the-hill); nothing else changed, matching revision-notes.r7.md's account. how-to-go-down (lines ~within draft) now targets jump-in-fast -> the-quick-slip and go-down-slow -> the-slow-slip instead of the-fall; last-look-at-the-gate now targets trust-the-cat -> the-slow-slip and go-anyway -> the-quick-slip. Both new passages open by honoring the predecessor's chosen action before the wet-rim slip defeats it: the-quick-slip opens 'Eli did not wait. He was ready for jumping in, fast and bold. But the rim was wet. His feet slid before he could jump at all.' (matches 'Jump in fast, feet first' / 'Decide to follow the cat anyway'); the-slow-slip opens 'Eli trusted the cat. He went slow, climbing down with care. But the rim was wet too. His foot slid, and down he went anyway.' (matches 'Ease yourself down slowly instead' / 'Trust the cat and climb down'). Neither choice label is denied by the text it leads to any more.

the-quick-slip and the-slow-slip are genuinely different reads, not reworded copies of each other or of the-fall: 'a quick spin, faster than he had planned' / landing 'with a squelch' (the-quick-slip) versus 'a slow spin, gentler than he had planned' / landing 'with a splash' (the-slow-slip), on top of the differing opening beats quoted above. A second read through how-to-go-down or last-look-at-the-gate reaches visibly different text each time, satisfying the acceptance criterion that choices give different routes on a second read. Downstream, both new passages end with the same two choices as the-fall (look-around[-quick/-slow] -> varro; check-bag[-quick/-slow] -> check-the-book), so items (reed-net), clues (claw-prints) and all five endings are unaffected -- confirmed by the diff showing no other passage changed.

the-fall itself is untouched (byte-identical to r6) and still serves its other four predecessors: through-the-gap's 'lean-over' (Lean over the edge to look down), call-to-the-cat's 'lean-after-call' (Lean over the rim and look), the-gate's 'lean-over-gate' (Lean over the edge to look down), and call-for-help's 'lean-after-call-help' (Crouch down and look into the hole). All four describe leaning or crouching to peer into the hole, not a deliberate jump or climb, so the-fall's accidental-slip opening ('The rim was wet. Eli's shoe slid, and down he went.') remains consistent with all four, and check-the-book's generic 'mud' framing works for any of the three slip variants.

Routes traced against story.r7.json and graph.r7.json (choice ids; graph.r7.json's edge list contains no cycle, verified programmatically, so no route revisits an earlier passage): (1) ending-warm-den via the new jump-in-fast branch: late-for-school--squeeze-through-->through-the-gap--call-first-->call-to-the-cat--weigh-the-drop-->how-to-go-down--jump-in-fast-->the-quick-slip--look-around-quick-->varro--meet-lira-->meet-lira--take-stairs-->the-stairs--study-prints-->the-prints [+claw-prints]--up-after-prints-->tower-hall--climb-ladder-->ladder-climb--up-ladder-->lantern-room--offer-den (clue held)-->ending-warm-den. (2) ending-home-too-soon via the new trust-the-cat branch: late-for-school--try-the-gate-->the-gate--shout-for-help-->call-for-help--last-look-->last-look-at-the-gate--trust-the-cat-->the-slow-slip--look-around-slow-->varro--look-moss-->look-at-the-moss--watch-hill-->watch-the-hill--wave-first-->meet-lira--take-marsh-->the-marsh--hop-stones-->stone-hop--to-stairs-fast-->the-stairs--keep-climbing-->tower-hall--ask-home-->home-too-soon. (3)-(5) ending-drum-song, ending-the-grab and ending-two-heads are each one choice from lantern-room (tap-drum / grab-stone / ask-lira) and reachable from any upstream route, matching graph.r7.json's reachableEndings (5/5, stateSearchComplete: true). All five endings reachable; no item or clue referenced before it is granted.

The watch-the-hill literacy fix is consistent with its scene: look-at-the-moss says 'A girl was running down the hill', varro's choice label says 'Wave to the girl running down the hill', and watch-the-hill (r7) now says 'Eli watched the girl, still running, come closer down the hill' -- restoring the dropped -ing form and reconciling the grammar as the r6 literacy review requested, without introducing a new inconsistency.

findings.message: Carried over from review-6-qa, unchanged in r7 (confirmed by diff -- none of these six passages were touched this revision): both choices in each of these round-2 connector passages rejoin the same next passage with no visible acknowledgement of which choice was taken, so they read as decorative forks that satisfy the graph validator's 'at least two choices' rule rather than genuine branches. Not a contradiction like the two r6 majors, and per the coordinator's prior instruction this is optional and non-blocking; re-flagging as minor for a future narrative pass, not as a blocker for this revision.

I ran `npm run check` myself. Lint, typecheck, 191 unit tests, and the build step all pass. `npm run validate:stories` still fails overall (exit code 1), for the same pre-existing, unrelated reason flagged in review-6-qa: public/stories/previews/the-cat-who-took-the-wrong-turn.json is a stale demo/preview snapshot at story version 4 (20 passages) with the same nine single-choice errors, not this job's draft (story v7, 40 passages). `git status` confirms that preview file is untracked-clean (not modified by this revision) and `git log -1` shows it was last committed well before this job's recent revisions. The same validate:stories run independently fails on three other unrelated jobs' stale preview snapshots (the-derelict-salvage, wake-cycle), confirming this is a repo-wide staleness issue outside this job's scope, not something introduced here. This job's own automated-validation gate, reports/validation.r7.json, is ok: true with schema ok, graph ok (5/5 endings reachable), literacy checks ok, and brief ok (only the pre-existing 3-sentence-length warning) -- verified directly against story.r7.json. I am not claiming npm run check passes for the repository as a whole; that failure should stay escalated to the orchestrator/release-manager separately from this story's content review, as review-6-qa already noted.

Content integrity: a full-text scan of story.r7.json's passages and choice labels found no sexual material, violence/gore, suicide/self-harm or religious references, matching brief.json's continuity.avoid list. Characters, setting and facts (Eli, Ash, Lira, the Lantern Tower, the land of Varro, Eli wanting to go home) are consistent throughout, including in the two new passages. reports/validation.r7.json confirms all three word sets (blend-words 94/10, closed-syllable-words 63/8, ing-words 27/8) meet their minOccurrences and appear on the shortest route to every ending (word-sets-on-every-route: ok), and all three target concepts are present with no concept mismatches -- matching revision-notes.r7.md's claim of 27 ing-word occurrences and an 8-12 per-ending-route range. Pre-existing, non-blocking, unchanged since r4/r6: three sentences (late-for-school, frog-helped, home-too-soon) remain one word over the brief's 16-word soft limit; this is a literacy-stage concern, not a QA blocker, and revision-notes.r7.md correctly scoped it out of this revision.
